original.description: A line of French infantry running forward with rifles and fixed bayonets across open grass — képis, dark-blue capotes buttoned back, the pantalon rouge hidden by the coats — photographed by the Agence Rol at the Grandes manœuvres of 1913. An exercise, not a battle: the photograph is widely reproduced and miscaptioned as the Marne or the Frontiers of 1914.

colorization.status: ok — label 'colorized (AI-assisted)'; documented colours: dark-blue capotes and képis (the red képi band and red trousers of 1914 are largely hidden), brown leather, summer grass. Colour-check: plausible for 1913 field dress.

caption: French infantry charging with the bayonet at the Grandes manœuvres of 1913 — the army of Plan XVII a year before it attacked into Lorraine and the Ardennes in the same coats and képis. A peacetime exercise, often miscaptioned as the Marne. Colorized (AI-assisted) from an Agence Rol photograph.
credit: Original photograph: Agence Rol, 1913; Bibliothèque nationale de France, Gallica (btv1b6931787b), via Wikimedia Commons; public domain. Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Provided by Dave 2026-08-22 (original linked from the Marne Wikipedia article).
